parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Hi, Dean, did you have a good weekend?
Yes, it was good to relax after a whole week of teaching practice. I really enjoyed the experience, though.
Yes, so did I. And I think it went well anyway. Are you okay to talk about the report we've got to write on the geography lesson we taught together? I was thinking we could make notes now and then divide the actual writing up between us.
Sure, good idea. Let's begin with our lesson name, shall we?
Right. Well, I know the main one was getting the class to think about how people in different parts of the world are connected to each other through the things they buy and sell.
Yes, we took that from the syllabus for Grade 4. And then we decided to use pencils as our example because they're relatively simple in design and everyone's used a pencil at some time or other. We should include that information too, right?
And we also wanted to get the class thinking about how things are moved around the world in different ways, from the farms and the mines to the factories and then the stores. That wasn't in the core syllabus. I think we added that ourselves.
Yes, I think you're right. Okay.
Then the last section of the report contains a post-lesson analysis.
We have to mention any problems we identified in our lesson when we taught it. So, any ideas?
Well, I know we were really satisfied with our handouts and worksheets. We both thought they'd been at just the right level for the class. And I don't know about you, but I think we worked well as a team.
Absolutely. Neither of us was too dominant, and we supported each other. Personally, the thing I think we didn't get right was the way we paced things. Some things seemed to be rushed and others seemed to drag on too long. I don't know how you feel about that.
The same as you. If we did the same lesson again, I'd want to make some adjustments to that, but keep the same basic lesson plan.
Okay, we see eye to eye on that. But there's one other thing. At the time, I seem to remember, we both thought that organising the children in sets of six didn't work very well, and that pairs would have been better for certain tasks so that the shyer kids got more chance to contribute.
Yes, I remember that too, and we should put it into our report as well.
Now, should we go over our lesson plan together before we write the report? It seems ages ago now.
Fine. Well, the whole lesson was based on the production and distribution of pencils. First, we gave out the pencils and got the students to decide what they're made of. Then, when they'd come up with all five of the component materials, we talked about which countries produce most of these materials.
Oh, yes. And we got volunteers to come to the front and mark the location of those on a map of the world. I remember they were really keen to volunteer. We had to stop them from calling the answers out loud.
Right. Then we brainstormed all the different ways of getting goods from one place to another and what the advantages and disadvantages of each one would be. I remember one girl talking about using horses.
That's right. She seemed to be a bit stuck in the past. It was hard not to smile.
Yes. After that, we put them in small groups, and each group represented one of the countries on the map. They had to use their atlas to decide an itinerary for sending their raw materials to the USA, specifying the different ports and places on the way there.
That's right. And by the time they'd done that, it was break time.
And after the break, they had to imagine they were pencil manufacturers in Chicago and fill in details on a worksheet about how they dispatch their pencils to different parts of the country.
Oh, yes, okay.
And then we had a class discussion about whether people will still be using pencils in 2050 and whether the design of pencils is likely to change. And to round the lesson off, the kids had to spend 10 minutes planning a short presentation for another class about possible developments. And that was it.
Good. So I'll write up that part.

analyses.content: 男生提到主要目的是让学生思考世界各地的人们是如何通过“买卖东西（buy and sell）”相互联系的，这对应了“全球相互依存（global interdependency）”。
Right. Well, I know the main one was getting the class to think about how people in different parts of the world are connected to each other through the things they buy and sell.
你可能听到“pencil”就想选 E（书写工具的发展），但铅笔只是用来举例的“道具”，不是课程的教学目标。

女生补充说，他们想让学生思考物品是如何以不同方式“在世界各地移动（moved around the world）”的，这对应了“运输系统（transport systems）”。

男生回忆说，当时他们都觉得把孩子分成“六人一组（sets of six）”效果不好，应该用双人组，这属于“学生分组”的问题。

不要听到 lesson plan 就想选 C（课程结构），录音后面紧接着说如果要重做，会保持“同样的基本教案（same basic lesson plan）”，说明结构没问题。
女生说她觉得没做好的地方是“节奏（paced things）”，有的太快有的拖太久，这对应选项中的 timing（时间把控）。

Geography lesson plan: student activities
Examine a pencil and discuss where the component materials come from.
⬇
Locate the top on a world map.
⬇
Discuss the pros and cons of different .
⬇
In groups, discuss countries' possible to the USA.

analyses.content: Then, when they'd come up with all five of the component materials, we talked about which countries produce most of these materials. Oh, yes. And we got volunteers to come to the front and mark the location of those on a map of the world.
你可能听到 materials 就想填，但题目问的是 locate（定位）的对象，定位的是国家（生产者），而不是材料本身。
录音说谈论完材料后，让志愿者在地图上标出“生产大部分材料的国家（countries produce most of these materials）”，即标出“生产商（producers）”。
录音提到头脑风暴了将货物从一地运到另一地的“不同方式（different ways）”及其优缺点，对应选项 H 的“运输方法”。

Right. Then we brainstormed all the different ways of getting goods from one place to another and what the advantages and disadvantages of each one would be. I remember one girl talking about using horses.
虽然录音里有个女孩提到了 horses（马），但这只是一个具体的例子，你要归纳出整体是在讲“运输方式”。
They had to use their atlas to decide an itinerary for sending their raw materials to the USA, specifying the different ports and places on the way there.
听到 itinerary 这个词要反应过来它是 route 的同义替换，指具体的行进路线。
录音说学生要决定将原材料送到美国的“行程路线（itinerary）”，这对应选项 A 的“出口路线（export routes）”。
And after the break, they had to imagine they were pencil manufacturers in Chicago and fill in details on a worksheet about how they dispatch their pencils to different parts of the country.
这题很直接，只要听到 fill in details on a... 就能抓住 worksheet，别被后面的 dispatch（发货）干扰。
录音非常直接地说，学生要在一个“工作表（worksheet）”上填写细节。
And then we had a class discussion about whether people will still be using pencils in 2050 and whether the design of pencils is likely to change.
你可能听到 design（设计）就想找相关选项，但这里讨论的是 design 是否会改变，核心话题是未来的情况。
录音提到讨论了人们在“2050年”是否还会用铅笔，这显然是关于“未来（future）”的讨论。
And to round the lesson off, the kids had to spend 10 minutes planning a short presentation for another class about possible developments.
Presentation 和 Talk 是雅思听力中非常经典的同义替换，不要因为没听到 talk 这个词就选错成 homework。
录音最后说孩子们要计划一个简短的“展示（presentation）”，这对应选项 C 的“谈话/演讲（talk）”。
